title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and says it’s up to 45 percent cheaper for agentic work
content:
Anthropic says its newest AI models, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, address criticisms from customers about price, data retention, and overzealous safeguards. The company claims Claude Fable 5.1 offers stronger performance than Fable 5, but costs around 25 percent less typically and up to 45 percent less for complex agentic tasks, thanks to reduced pricing on cached data that was already processed and stored.
Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and says it’s up to 45 percent cheaper for agentic work
Mythos 5.1 is also launching in Project Glasswing.
Along with the announcement, a slew of early impressions popped up, including from Every CEO Dan Shipper, who claims, “It’s the strongest coding model we’ve used, but now it’s fast, token-efficient, and crucially actually speaks like a normal person.”
Box CEO Aaron Levie is another early access believer, saying that his company’s agent with Fable 5.1 picked up on subtleties and ambiguities in data that Fable 5 missed in the same test. Meanwhile, Lisan al Gaib points out that on benchmarks, Mythos 5.1 with low reasoning scores the same as its predecessor set to Max reasoning.
Fable 5.1 also has “more precise safeguards” that Anthropic says are less likely to block basic biology questions than Fable 5, but Mythos 5.1 has the same biology restrictions as the previous model. Anthropic also explained its progress on data retention, saying that Enterprise Frontier Safeguards offer “complete privacy” by storing data on the customer’s cloud servers instead of its own, and will start rolling out later this fall.
Anthropic says it’s “now allowing Fable 5.1 to be used for identifying software vulnerabilities,” but it will still redirect some cybersecurity tasks to Opus models, like “penetration testing, exploit generation, and binary-based vulnerability scanning.” Claude Fable 5.1 is now available on all platforms, while Mythos 5.1 is available to Project Glasswing participants only.

report.summary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 with up to 45% lower agentic costs, improved safeguards, and expanded platform availability.
report.background: The release comes as Anthropic faces growing customer complaints about cost, strict safety filters, and data retention practices. Fable 5.1 directly targets those pain points, with cheaper pricing on cached data, more precise safeguards that still block some sensitive topics, and a new enterprise privacy mode that keeps customer data on the customer’s own cloud servers. Early access users, including executives from Every and Box, report strong gains in coding quality, token efficiency, and agentic nuance, suggesting the model is tuned for practical, production-level workflows rather than just benchmark scores. The move also places pressure on competitors like OpenAI and Google to respond with similarly aggressive pricing and privacy features as enterprises increasingly deploy AI agents.
key_points: Fable 5.1 is about 25 percent cheaper on typical usage and up to 45 percent cheaper for complex agentic work. The savings come largely from reduced pricing on cached data that has already been processed, making repeated agentic loops more affordable for enterprises.

Early impressions highlight major coding gains. Every CEO Dan Shipper called it the strongest coding model his team has used, and Box CEO Aaron Levie said its agent caught subtle ambiguities in data that Fable 5 missed, indicating better real-world reasoning and token efficiency.

Safeguards are more granular than before. Anthropic says Fable 5.1 is less likely to block basic biology questions, though Mythos 5.1 keeps the same biology restrictions. Fable 5.1 can now identify software vulnerabilities, but exploit generation and penetration testing are still redirected to Opus models.

Enterprise data retention is addressed through new Frontier Safeguards. This feature stores data on customer cloud servers rather than Anthropic’s infrastructure, promising complete privacy and rolling out later this fall to meet enterprise compliance needs.

Mythos 5.1 launches only inside Project Glasswing, while Fable 5.1 is widely available. Notably, Mythos 5.1 with low reasoning scores matches its predecessor at maximum reasoning, suggesting efficiency gains for different task types.
report.impact: This release moves the AI industry toward price-driven competition for agentic work. Cutting cached token costs makes multi-step AI agents dramatically cheaper to operate, which could accelerate enterprise adoption of autonomous workflows. Developers gain a coding model that is both powerful and token-efficient, reducing infrastructure spend and latency in production. For regular users, the refined safeguards may mean fewer frustrating blocks, though restricted cybersecurity tasks and Mythos biology limits show Anthropic still drawing safety lines. The Enterprise Frontier Safeguards privacy mode also shifts how AI providers handle sensitive data, potentially setting a new expectation for data sovereignty in enterprise AI deployments.
report.tools: Developers can explore Anthropic's API and prompt caching documentation to take advantage of lower cached-token pricing. Claude Code remains a useful CLI for coding workflows, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) is worth watching for building agentic systems. Open-source agent frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex can also help test Fable 5.1’s reasoning and cost efficiency in custom applications.
